small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune tiles (BLOCK_OC=128/BLOCK_SP=128 with num_warps=8, num_stages=2/3) and try BLOCK_OC=64/BLOCK_SP=256 to amortize the K-loop overhead; with OH*OW=64516 and OC=64 we have plenty of work per program.
- Swap the program-id ordering so `pid_sp` is the fastest-varying outer axis or pack `(N, OC tile)` into one axis to improve L2 reuse of the weight tile across the N=128 dimension — weights are tiny (64*72*4B) and currently re-fetched per (n, oc) program.
- Precompute `oh*IW` and reuse `kh*IW + kw` offsets outside the K-loop; consider using `tl.multiple_of`/`tl.max_contiguous` hints on `sp_offs` so input loads vectorize along the contiguous W axis.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a persistent kernel that tiles output spatially in 2D (BLOCK_OH × BLOCK_OW) instead of flattening OH*OW; this makes the input gather contiguous along W (coalesced 128-byte loads) and lets the kh/kw loop reuse halo rows in registers/shared memory across kw.
- Move to a NHWC (channels-last) layout for both input and output so the GEMM-K axis (IC*KH*KW) has IC contiguous; with IC=8 the inner-K dim becomes a clean vector load and `tl.dot` operands align naturally without the current k-decomposition arithmetic.
- Consider an explicit unroll of the KH*KW=9 loop (KH, KW are constexpr) with IC as the only runtime K-reduction inside `tl.dot`; this turns the kernel into 9 small GEMMs accumulating into the same tile, eliminating the integer divmod for ic/kh/kw and letting the compiler schedule loads better.
